Build piecewise regression coding for single-case design phases

Source: R/utils-data.R
process_scd_phases.Rd

Adds level, trend, and slope-change columns suitable for a piecewise multilevel model with time-series intervention coding inside a three-level meta-analytic structure. Every change point is coded within each tier (the combination of the columns returned by tier_vars()) at that tier's own onset, using the actual time values, so unequally spaced sessions and staggered onsets are honored.

Usage

process_scd_phases(data, structure, scd_type = "reversal")

Arguments

data

A data frame with a phase column.

structure

A list describing the hierarchical structure.

scd_type

Design type: "reversal", "multiple_baseline", "multiple_probe", "alternating" (alias "alternating_treatment"), "changing_criterion", or "AB".

Value

The data frame with piecewise regression columns added, rows in the input order.

Details

AB, multiple baseline, multiple probe. time_A = t - T_A on every row, where T_A is the first baseline time of the tier, so the intercept is the expected level at the start of baseline and time_A carries the baseline trend through all phases. level_AB is 1 from the first intervention time T_B on and trend_AB = (t - T_B) * level_AB, so level_AB is the immediate change at T_B relative to the projected baseline line and trend_AB the change in slope. Maintenance and generalization phases add level_BM/trend_BM and level_BG/trend_BG coded the same way from their own onsets: the first maintenance-role time and the first generalization-role time, so an A-B-G tier carries no maintenance step and level_BG is the change at the generalization onset. time_B, time_M, time_G hold t minus the corresponding onset on every row. Phases absent from a tier are coded 0.

Reversal (ABAB, BAB, ABA, ABABAB). Labels with a known role (see phase_role(), including numeric codes 0/1/2/3 and numbered labels such as "Baseline 1" or "A_2") are renamed to the role letters A, B, M, G; other labels keep their letters. Runs are then numbered by occurrence within the tier (A1, B1, A2, B2, M1). The first-run time (time_<first run>) is t - T_1 on every row of the tier. Each transition into run k adds a cumulative step level_<prev><next> = 1[t >= T_k] (step coding) and a continuing slope change trend_<prev><next> = (t - T_k) * 1[t >= T_k]. This is the centered ABAB model: each level coefficient is the change between adjacent phases at the first observation of the later phase, and each trend coefficient the change in slope between adjacent phases. When tiers start in different phases (an ABAB tier next to a BAB tier), every first-run time column is kept (0 on the other tiers) and a warning notes that the onset steps differ across tiers and are estimated separately.

Changing criterion. time_A = t - T_A on every row. Each criterion subphase j (split on a numeric criterion, crit, criterion_level, or criterion_value column when present, otherwise on phase-label runs) adds a cumulative step level_crit<j> = 1[t >= T_cj] and a continuing trend_crit<j> = (t - T_cj) * level_crit<j>, so each step compares adjacent subphases. A return to an earlier criterion opens a new subphase. A return to baseline after a criterion subphase adds the step level_ret<k> = 1[t >= T_rk]. Without any baseline phase, time_A runs from the first session of the tier and level_crit1/trend_crit1 are dropped with a warning, since they would equal the intercept and time_A. The collapsed treatment (intervention vs baseline) column is an intervention indicator; time_treatment = (t - T_c1) * treatment is a centered variant of an uncentered session-number time variable.

Alternating treatments. The first baseline-role condition (else the first condition) is the reference; every other condition, including a second baseline-role label such as "Control", gets a dummy atd_<condition>. The atd_ prefix keeps data columns such as treatment_fidelity out of the condition terms. A general session trend time_session = t - T_1, the session time centered at the first session of the tier; centering at the first session only shifts the intercept. Without it, a general trend loads on the condition dummies whenever conditions are unevenly spread over time. Alternation blocks are counted within each tier.

The time column is structure$time_vars[1] when supplied, otherwise find_time_var() (case-insensitive); with neither, sessions are numbered in row order within each tier, with a warning that concurrence across tiers cannot be assessed.

Examples

d <- simulate_scd_data(n_cases = 2, n_phase_a = 5, n_phase_b = 5)
process_scd_phases(d, structure = list(), scd_type = "AB")
